raw_case_text:
A 46 year-old African-American woman with HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy (ART) presented to the National Institutes of Health (NIH) from a community health center in Washington, DC, for further evaluation of elevated LAEs. Her baseline CD4 cell count was 420 cells/mm3 and her LAEs were normal prior to starting ART (Figure 1). Five months after initiation of ART with the fixed-dose combination pill of efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine, routine laboratory evaluation revealed a mild increase in her serum alkaline phosphatase (AP) to 207 U/L (normal < 116 U/L). Her AP briefly normalized before increasing again, followed by progressive increases in aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT) over the next year. Her CD4 cell count increased to 1,100 cells/mm3, with suppression of her HIV viral load from 62,000 copies/mL (log 4.8) to <50 copies/mL within the first 3 months of ART and remained stable thereafter.
On evaluation at the NIH, she complained of mild right upper quadrant pain and denied any other symptom. She reported a family history of scleroderma. She denied known drug allergies, over-the-counter medication use, herbal or dietary supplementation, alcohol abuse or illicit drug use. Screening laboratories showed elevation in her LAEs with AST 244 U/L, ALT 287 U/L, AP of 659 U/L, and gamma glutamyl transferase (GGT) of 607 U/L (Figure 1). Serum total bilirubin peaked at 1.7mg/dL (direct bilirubin 1.3mg/dL). Viral hepatitis serologies, hepatitis B DNA PCR and hepatitis C RNA PCR were negative. Serum iron and ceruloplasmin and alpha-1 antitrypsin levels were normal.
Autoantibody testing was remarkable for a positive ANA, greater than 12.0EU (negative < 1EU, positive > or = 1EU, strongly positive > or = 3EU) and a positive anti-mitochondrial antibody, greater than 0.6U, (negative <0.1U). Anti-smooth muscle antibody and anti-liver-kidney microsomal antibody were negative. Serum copper was elevated slightly above the upper limit of normal (173 mcg/dL, normal <145 mcg/dL). Subsequent laboratory testing revealed hypergammaglobulinemia (serum IgG 5,250 mg/dL, normal <1730 mg/dL), positive anti-centromere (>8.0 U, negative <0.1U) and anti-double stranded DNA (799 IU/mL, normal <30 IU/mL) antibodies. SCL-70 antibodies were negative. Abdominal ultrasound and triple-phase CT scan of the liver were normal.
Percutaneous liver biopsy showed chronic cholestatic liver disease with marked inflammatory activity, bile duct injury, and periportal and perivenular fibrosis consistent with primary biliary cirrhosis (Figure 2). Immunohistochemistry staining for cytokeratin 7 was performed using anti-cytokeratin 7 antibody from Dako (clone OV-TL-12/30 at 1:400 dilution) and the Ventana Ultra View detection system. Based on this histology and supporting laboratory findings of hypergammaglobulinemia, positive anti-nuclear and anti-mitochondrial antibodies, the patient was diagnosed with primary biliary cirrhosis and autoimmune hepatitis overlap syndrome.
Treatment was initiated with oral prednisone (30mg daily for 7 days, then 20mg daily) and ursodiol (13-15 mg/kg daily). She continued efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine. After one month of treatment, prednisone was tapered with concomitant initiation of azathioprine (150mg daily). Her LAEs improved over the next year (Figure 1). Elevated IgG fraction declined. Her CD4 count has remained stable, and she is in excellent clinical condition.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old African American woman with HIV infection on antiretroviral therapy was referred to the National Institutes of Health for evaluation of mild right upper quadrant abdominal pain and progressive cholestatic and hepatocellular liver enzyme elevations.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: With normal baseline liver-associated enzymes (LAEs) and a CD4+ count of 420 cells/mm3 prior to starting fixed-dose efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine, the patient developed a mild alkaline phosphatase elevation (207 U/L) 5 months after ART initiation, followed over the ensuing year by progressive marked increases in alkaline phosphatase, GGT, AST, and ALT alongside mild right upper quadrant discomfort, while achieving full HIV viral suppression (<50 copies/mL) and robust CD4 recovery to 1,100 cells/mm3.
subjective.past_medical_history: HIV infection well controlled on efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine. Family history notable for scleroderma. Denied alcohol abuse, illicit drug use, over-the-counter medications, or herbal/dietary supplements.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mild right upper quadrant abdominal pain; negative for jaundice or other constitutional symptoms. Home medication: fixed-dose efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine. No known drug allergies.

objective.routine_investigations: NIH laboratory evaluation showed AST 244 U/L, ALT 287 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 659 U/L (normal <116 U/L), GGT 607 U/L, peak total bilirubin 1.7 mg/dL (direct bilirubin 1.3 mg/dL), and slightly elevated serum copper (173 µg/dL; normal <145 µg/dL). Viral hepatitis serologies, HBV DNA PCR, HCV RNA PCR, serum iron, ceruloplasmin, and alpha-1 antitrypsin were all normal/negative. Autoimmune workup revealed marked hypergammaglobulinemia (serum IgG 5,250 mg/dL; normal <1,730 mg/dL), strongly positive ANA (>12.0 EU; strongly positive >=3 EU), positive anti-mitochondrial antibody (AMA >0.6 U; negative <0.1 U), positive anti-centromere antibody (>8.0 U; negative <0.1 U), and elevated anti-dsDNA antibody (799 IU/mL; normal <30 IU/mL), with negative anti-smooth muscle, anti-LKM, and anti-Scl-70 antibodies. Abdominal ultrasound was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-cell count had increased from 420 cells/mm3 pre-ART to 1,100 cells/mm3. Triple-phase liver CT was normal. Percutaneous liver biopsy with cytokeratin 7 (CK7) immunohistochemistry demonstrated chronic cholestatic liver disease with florid interface/lobular hepatitis, bile duct injury, and periportal and perivenular fibrosis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Autoimmune immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (autoimmune IRIS) manifesting as primary biliary cirrhosis / autoimmune hepatitis (PBC/AIH) overlap syndrome in a 46-year-old African American woman following robust CD4+ T-cell reconstitution (from 420 to 1,100 cells/mm3) and HIV viral suppression (from 62,000 to <50 copies/mL) on efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine. Confirmed by percutaneous liver biopsy showing combined bile duct injury and marked interface hepatitis alongside AMA >0.6 U, ANA >12.0 EU, anti-dsDNA 799 IU/mL, and IgG 5,250 mg/dL. She was treated with oral ursodiol (13–15 mg/kg/day) and oral prednisone (30 mg daily for 7 days, then 20 mg daily for 1 month before tapering) transitioned to maintenance azathioprine (150 mg daily) while continuing efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine, achieving normalization of liver enzymes and IgG levels and stable CD4 counts over 1 year of follow-up.
